title: RPG Design Guides: Rules for Writing and Displaying Text

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】文章の記述・表示におけるルール
blocks.translation: RPG Design Guides: Rules for Writing and Displaying Text

blocks.source: 物語の脚本を書く前に、文章を記述・表示するルールを決めておきたい。これを決めないままにシナリオを書いていると、統一感がなく、読み辛い文章になってしまうかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Before writing the script for your story, you should decide on rules for writing and displaying text. If you write the scenario without deciding on these rules first, the text may lack consistency and become difficult to read.

blocks.source: 特に経験が浅い制作者は、スタイルがまだ固まっていないと思われるので要注意。ポイントとなる部分を以下にまとめるので、何も考えていなかったという箇所があれば、参考にして頂ければ。
blocks.translation: This is especially important for less experienced creators, whose style may not yet be fully established. I have summarized the key points below, so please use them as a reference if there are any areas you had not given much thought to.

blocks.source: セリフを表記する際のルール
blocks.translation: Rules for Formatting Dialogue

blocks.source: 登場人物にセリフを喋らせる場合、小説でもゲームでも通常は「」（カギ括弧）を使用する。言うまでもない基本事項だけど、たまに『：』もあったりする。ゲームの場合は閉じる側の括弧『」』は省略することも。
blocks.translation: When having characters speak dialogue, quotation marks are normally used in both novels and games. This is an obvious basic rule, but occasionally you may also see a colon used. In games, the closing quotation mark is sometimes omitted.

blocks.source: 以下にいくつかセリフの書き方の例を挙げてみる。
blocks.translation: Here are a few examples of ways to write dialogue.

blocks.source: 話し手
blocks.translation: Speaker

blocks.source: 「ここはＸＸＸＸの町です。
blocks.translation: “This is the town of XXXX.

blocks.source: 北に行くと、塔がありますよ。
blocks.translation: If you head north, you’ll find a tower.

blocks.source: 話し手「ここはＸＸＸＸの町です。
blocks.translation: Speaker: “This is the town of XXXX.

blocks.source: 北に行くと、塔がありますよ。
blocks.translation: If you head north, you’ll find a tower.

blocks.source: 話し手
blocks.translation: Speaker

blocks.source: 「ここはＸＸＸＸの町です。
blocks.translation: “This is the town of XXXX.

blocks.source: 北に行くと、塔がありますよ。
blocks.translation: If you head north, you’ll find a tower.

blocks.source: 【話し手】
blocks.translation: 【Speaker】

blocks.source: 「ここはＸＸＸＸの町です。北に行くと、塔がありますよ。ついでに言うと、東には森がありますよ。
blocks.translation: “This is the town of XXXX. If you head north, you’ll find a tower. By the way, there’s a forest to the east as well.

blocks.source: 話し手の名前を表示した後に、改行するかしないかは、作品によって異なる。僕としては改行する方がお勧め。その方が読みやすいし、話し手の名前が長くても文章のバランスが崩れない。セリフ中のどこに改行を入れるかも重要。メッセージウインドウの端までセリフを改行しないという手法もある。
blocks.translation: Whether or not to insert a line break after displaying the speaker’s name varies from one work to another. Personally, I recommend inserting one. It makes the text easier to read, and the balance of the text does not fall apart even when the speaker’s name is long. Where to insert line breaks within dialogue is also important. Another technique is to avoid inserting a line break until the dialogue reaches the edge of the message window.

blocks.source: 小説ではできない、ゲームならではの手法として、話し手の文字色を変えたりもできる。見やすいように工夫してみよう。
blocks.translation: As a technique unique to games that is not possible in novels, you can also change the color of the speaker’s text. Try devising a clear and easy-to-read presentation.

blocks.source: その他文章を表記する際のルール
blocks.translation: Rules for Formatting Other Text

blocks.source: セリフを「」で表記する事は既に当然のルールとなっている。しかし、セリフ以外――例えば『ナレーション』『書物』『思考』等を表記する場合はどうすれば良いだろうか？
blocks.translation: Using quotation marks for dialogue has already become an established rule. But what should you do when displaying things other than dialogue—for example, narration, books, or thoughts?

blocks.source: それには、
blocks.translation: One option is to use symbols such as

blocks.source: 等の記号を使用する方法がある。
blocks.translation: these.

blocks.source: 例えば、主人公の思考は……
blocks.translation: For example, the protagonist’s thoughts could be shown as…

blocks.source: ＞そっとしておこう
blocks.translation: > Let’s leave it alone

blocks.source: 書物や看板などの読み物は……
blocks.translation: For readable text such as books and signs…

blocks.source: ”毒の沼地。危険入るな！
blocks.translation: ”Poison marsh. Danger! Keep out!

blocks.source: というように記述する。あるいは"「"が無い場合はナレーション……という様に記号を用いないこと自体を目印としてもＯＫ。
blocks.translation: This is one way to write it. Alternatively, if there is no opening quotation mark, you can use the absence of a symbol itself as a marker to indicate narration.

blocks.source: また、記号を使用しなくても、メッセージウインドウの形を変えるという手法もある。漫画で吹き出しの形を変えるのは一般的な手法だが、ゲームでもライブアライブ等がやっている。セリフであっても、絶叫や囁き、テレパシーなどを区別して表記することもできる。
blocks.translation: Another technique is to change the shape of the message window instead of using symbols. Changing the shape of speech balloons is a common technique in manga, and games such as Live A Live use it as well. Even for dialogue, you can distinguish between shouts, whispers, telepathy, and so on through the formatting.
【Example】

blocks.source: ナレーション → 黒背景
blocks.translation: Narration → Black background

blocks.source: 絶叫 → ギザギザウインドウ（下の吹き出しみたいなヤツ）
blocks.translation: Shout → Jagged window (like the speech balloon below)

blocks.source: 思考 → モコモコウインドウ（。o O ○）
blocks.translation: Thought → Fluffy window (。o O ○)

blocks.source: ＜くせ者だあッ！！ ＞
blocks.translation: <It’s a trap!! >

blocks.source: ↑環境によってはズレてるかも……。
blocks.translation: ↑ This may be misaligned depending on your environment…

blocks.source: 読点『、』の使い方
blocks.translation: How to Use the Comma ‘、’

blocks.source: 『、』を打つタイミングについて、実は明確なルールは存在しないらしい。適度に打つことで、読みやすい文章にしていこう。
blocks.translation: Apparently, there are no clear rules for when to use ‘、’. Use it appropriately to make your writing easier to read.

blocks.source: 例えば、『漢字で表記するかひらがなで表記するか』という文のように、ひらがな同士で言葉が繋がってしまう場合は区切りが分かりにくい。なので、筆者は特に意識して『、』を打って文を分けるようにしている。『漢字で表記するか、ひらがなで表記するか』という感じで。
blocks.translation: For example, in a sentence such as ‘whether to write it in kanji or hiragana,’ it can be difficult to tell where to pause when words written in hiragana run together. That is why I make a point of using ‘、’ to separate such sentences. In other words: ‘whether to write it in kanji, or whether to write it in hiragana.’

blocks.source: ゲームの場合『、』ではなく、『半角スペース』や『全角スペース』を使用することも。ちなみに僕は今のところ『半角スペース』派です。
blocks.translation: In games, you may use a half-width space or a full-width space instead of ‘、’. Personally, for now, I prefer half-width spaces.

blocks.source: 句点『。』の使い方
blocks.translation: How to Use the Period ‘。’

blocks.source: もちろん文章の最後に打つ。『、』と違って、こちらに悩むことは少ないはず。ただ意識していないとなかなか気付かないかもしれないけれど、一般小説では「」の末尾には『。』を打たないことが普通になっていたりする。セリフを右括弧で閉じる様にしているのならば、このルールに合わせた方が無難かも。
blocks.translation: Of course, you put it at the end of a sentence. Unlike ‘、’, this should be less confusing. However, you may not notice this unless you pay attention to it: in general novels, it has become common not to put ‘。’ at the end of dialogue enclosed in quotation marks. If you close dialogue with a quotation mark, it may be safest to follow this rule.
【Example】

blocks.source: 「今日はいい天気ですね。
blocks.translation: “The weather is nice today.

blocks.source: 明日も晴れるといいですね」
blocks.translation: I hope it’s sunny tomorrow too.”

blocks.source: 三点リーダ『…』と棒ダッシュ『―』の使い方
blocks.translation: How to Use the Ellipsis ‘…’ and Em Dash ‘―’

blocks.source: 一般的な小説のルールでは、『…』『―』共に偶数回連続で繋げて使用する。『……』『…………』『――』『――――』というようにだ。でもゲームや漫画だと『…』単体での使用も見かけたりする。
blocks.translation: According to the general rules for novels, both ‘…’ and ‘―’ are used consecutively an even number of times. For example: ‘……’, ‘…………’, ‘――’, and ‘――――’. In games and manga, however, you may also see ‘…’ used by itself.

blocks.source: この２つの使い道に付いては、分かるようで分からない人も多いと思う。一部使い道が重なる部分があるのが、またややこしい。そんなわけで、使い道をまとめてみた。
blocks.translation: I think many people understand what these two are used for—or think they do—but are not completely sure. It is even more confusing because some of their uses overlap. So, I have compiled their uses below.

blocks.source: 『…』のみが使える
blocks.translation: Uses Specific to ‘…’

blocks.source: 語尾を濁す：「たぶん、そうだと思うけど……」
blocks.translation: Trailing off: “I think that’s probably right, but……”

blocks.source: 弱々しく ：「俺は……もう駄目……だ」
blocks.translation: Weakly: “I……can’t……go on”
Silence: “……”

blocks.source: 『―』と比較すると、使い道が分かりやすいので、特に補足はいらないと思う。
blocks.translation: Compared to “―,” its uses are easier to understand, so I don't think any particular explanation is necessary.

blocks.source: 『―』のみが使える
blocks.translation: Only “―” can be used

blocks.source: 割込：先生「え～と、何か連絡事項がある方は――」生徒「はい！」
blocks.translation: Interruption: Teacher: “Um, if anyone has any announcements—” Student: “Yes!”

blocks.source: 引用：「この古文書によると――玉座の後ろを調べろ――とあるね」
blocks.translation: Quotation: “According to this ancient document, it says—‘Search behind the throne’—you know.”

blocks.source: 補足：俺は村長の家――それは村中で最も立派な建物だった――に向かった。
blocks.translation: Supplement: I headed for the village chief's house—it was the finest building in the village.

blocks.source: 『割込』は唯一『―』の安定した使いどころ。
blocks.translation: “Interruption” is the only reliable use for “―.”

blocks.source: 『引用』は””や『』で囲ったほうが分かりやすいかも。
blocks.translation: “Quotation” might be easier to understand if enclosed in quotation marks such as “ ” or ‘ ’.

blocks.source: 『補足』は文章の中に文章を挟む構造になる。（）と使い方が類似している。海外小説の翻訳で良く見かけるけど、これを多用した文章は読み辛い。使うぐらいなら文章構成を考え直したほうがよさそう。といっても、ゲームにはあんまり関係なさそうだけど。
blocks.translation: “Supplement” creates a structure in which one sentence is inserted into another. Its usage is similar to parentheses. You often see it in translations of foreign novels, but writing that uses it too much is difficult to read. Rather than use it excessively, it would probably be better to rethink the sentence structure. That said, it doesn't seem to have much to do with games.

blocks.source: 『…』『―』両方で使える
blocks.translation: Both “…” and “―” can be used

blocks.source: 間を置く：「……それで、結局どうしますか？」
blocks.translation: Pause: “……So, what are we going to do in the end?”

blocks.source: 文を繋ぐ：「神――いわゆるゴッドの思し召しなのです」
blocks.translation: Connecting sentences: “God—it is the will of what is commonly called God.”

blocks.source: 『間を置く』の例のように文頭に間を作ることもできる。話題を転換したい場合などで有効。個人的には、何でもかんでも『ウェイト処理』で間を作るよりは、『…』や『―』で間を表現してもらった方がテンポが良くなるので好き。
blocks.translation: As in the example under “Pause,” you can also create a pause at the beginning of a sentence. This is effective when, for example, you want to change the subject. Personally, I prefer expressing pauses with “…” or “―” because it gives the pacing a better flow than creating pauses with “Wait” processing for everything.

blocks.source: 『文を繋ぐ』は『、』に近い運用方法となる。溜めを作ることで、後の文章をより強調できる効果もある。
blocks.translation: “Connecting sentences” is used in a way similar to a comma. Creating a buildup can also emphasize the sentence that follows.

blocks.source: このパターンの場合、『…』『―』どちらでも良いのだけど、個人的な印象では『…』は弱々しく、『―』はスピーディな気がする。『…』と『―』の使い分けは明確に統一されているわけではなく、色々と曖昧。作家によっても用途に差がある。興味があるなら、プロの文章を読む時に気を付けてみるのがオススメ。
blocks.translation: In this pattern, either “…” or “―” is fine, but personally, I feel that “…” seems weak, while “―” feels speedy. There is no clearly standardized distinction between the uses of “…” and “―”; it is fairly ambiguous. Their uses also vary from writer to writer. If you're interested, I recommend paying attention to this when reading professional writing.

blocks.source: 感嘆符『！』と疑問符『？』の使い方
blocks.translation: How to use exclamation marks “!” and question marks “?”

blocks.source: 『…』『―』と比較して、こちらの使い道に悩む人は少ないと思うが、ついでに書いてみる。
blocks.translation: Compared to “…” and “―,” I don't think many people have trouble deciding how to use these, but I'll cover them while I'm at it.

blocks.source: 『！』は驚きや叫びを現す。「うわっ！」「お～い！！」など。２つ以上重ねて強調する事もある。『？』は疑問や困惑を現す。「どなたですか？」「はあっ？」など。２つ以上重ねることは少なめ。
blocks.translation: “!” expresses surprise or a shout, as in “Whoa!” or “Heeey!!” Two or more can also be repeated for emphasis. “?” expresses a question or confusion, as in “Who are you?” or “Huh?” Repeating it two or more times is less common.

blocks.source: 『！？』というように両方を合わせる方法も多用される。「おかしいだろ！？」「マジでっ！？」というように、驚き叫びながら、困惑しているという表現になる。『？！』は余り使わないが、驚きよりも困惑を強調したいとか、独自性を出したいとか、理由があるならどうぞ。
blocks.translation: Combining both, as in “!?,” is also frequently used. In expressions such as “That's not right!?” and “Seriously!?,” it conveys confusion while shouting in surprise. “?!” is not used as often, but if you have a reason—such as wanting to emphasize confusion more than surprise or to show originality—then go ahead.

blocks.source: 「図書館では静かに……！」「へっ……？」「信じられない……！？」というように『…』と組み合わせることもできる。意味合いが反対に近い『！』と『…』が共存している事に違和感を持つ人もあるかもしれないが、「声を張り上げてはいないが、強い感情を込めている」といったニュアンスだと思う。たぶん……。
blocks.translation: They can also be combined with “…” as in “Quiet in the library……!”, “Huh……?”, or “Unbelievable……!?”. Some people may find it odd for “!” and “…”—which have nearly opposite meanings—to coexist, but I think the nuance is something like “not raising one's voice, but expressing strong emotion.” Probably……

blocks.source: 漢字で書くか、書かないか？
blocks.translation: Should you write it in kanji or not?

blocks.source: 以下のような言葉は特に、人によって漢字で表記するか、ひらがなで表記するか意見が分かれる。なるべく方針は統一しておこう。
blocks.translation: With words like the following in particular, opinions differ from person to person on whether to write them in kanji or hiragana. Try to keep your policy consistent as much as possible.

blocks.source: ある（有る）
blocks.translation: to exist

blocks.source: くらい、ぐらい（位）
blocks.translation: about, approximately

blocks.source: こと（事）
blocks.translation: thing

blocks.source: ため（為）
blocks.translation: for, purpose

blocks.source: つく（付く）
blocks.translation: to attach

blocks.source: できる（出来る）
blocks.translation: can, be able to

blocks.source: ない（無い）
blocks.translation: not exist

blocks.source: など（等）
blocks.translation: etc., and so on

blocks.source: なに、なん（何）
blocks.translation: what

blocks.source: なる（成る）
blocks.translation: to become

blocks.source: よう（様）
blocks.translation: way, manner

blocks.source: よく（良く）
blocks.translation: often, well

blocks.source: わかる（分かる）
blocks.translation: to understand

blocks.source: わけ（訳）
blocks.translation: reason, means

blocks.source: 筆者は『事』や『様』の使い方によく迷う。ひらがなが続く文章の場合は漢字で、漢字が続く文章の場合はひらがなで打ちたくなる。こんな事を書いておいて何だが、統一するのは結構しんどい。いっそ、その場の雰囲気や気分で、あえて統一せずに開き直っても良いかもしれない。
blocks.translation: The writer often has trouble deciding how to use “thing” and “way.” When a sentence contains a long string of hiragana, I feel like typing them in kanji; when it contains a long string of kanji, I feel like typing them in hiragana. After writing all this, I have to admit that keeping things consistent is quite difficult. Perhaps it would be better to deliberately abandon consistency and go with the atmosphere or mood of the moment.

blocks.source: 難しい漢字を使うかどうか？
blocks.translation: Should you use difficult kanji?

blocks.source: 例えば、『未曾有（みぞう）』『顰蹙（ひんしゅく）』『翻す（ひるがえす）』のような、難しい漢字を使用するかどうか？ ＰＣだと、簡単に漢字変換ができてしまうが、なんでもかんでも変換してしまうのは考えもの。プレイヤーの対象年齢次第では、みぞう、ヒンシュクの様に、ひらがな、カタカナで表記する事も検討しよう。ただし、「これはみぞうの事態だ」という具合に、見栄えは悪いので注意したい。
blocks.translation: For example, should you use difficult kanji for words such as “unprecedented (mizō),” “disapproval (hinshuku),” and “retract (hirugaesu)”? On a PC, it is easy to convert words into kanji, but converting everything automatically is worth reconsidering. Depending on the target age of your players, consider writing them in hiragana or katakana, such as “mizō” and “hinshuku.” However, be careful: wording such as “This is a mizō situation” looks unattractive.

blocks.source: 未曾有 → 空前
blocks.translation: Unprecedented → unprecedented

blocks.source: 顰蹙 → 反感
blocks.translation: Disapproval → resentment

blocks.source: 翻す → 撤回する
blocks.translation: Retract → withdraw

blocks.source: 上記の様に、もう少し簡単な言葉に言い換える方法もある。フリガナを打てるならば、理想的なのだけれど、制作ツールの制約や手間の問題がある。
blocks.translation: As shown above, you can also rephrase these with somewhat simpler words. Adding furigana would be ideal, but there are issues involving the limitations of the development tool and the extra effort required.

blocks.source: まとめ
blocks.translation: Summary

blocks.source: 読みやすい文章を書くためには、ルールの策定が不可欠。ウインドウの形状や文字色など、ゲームならではの技法を活用するのも選択肢の一つ。何にせよ、自分なりのルールを決めておこう。制作の終盤で書式・文体の統一をするハメにならないように注意したい。
blocks.translation: Establishing rules is essential for writing easy-to-read text. Using techniques unique to games, such as window shapes and text colors, is another option. In any case, establish your own rules. Be careful not to end up having to unify the formatting and writing style near the end of development.

Even for dialogue, you can distinguish between shouts, whispers, telepathy, and so on through the formatting.

texts.↑環境によってはズレてるかも……。: ↑ This may be misaligned depending on your environment…
texts.『、』を打つタイミングについて、実は明確なルールは存在しないらしい。適度に打つこ: Apparently, there are no clear rules for when to use ‘、’. Use it appropriately to make your writing easier to read.
texts.例えば、『漢字で表記するかひらがなで表記するか』という文のように、ひらがな同士で: For example, in a sentence such as ‘whether to write it in kanji or hiragana,’ it can be difficult to tell where to pause when words written in hiragana run together. That is why I make a point of using ‘、’ to separate such sentences. In other words: ‘whether to write it in kanji, or whether to write it in hiragana.’
texts.ゲームの場合『、』ではなく、『半角スペース』や『全角スペース』を使用することも。: In games, you may use a half-width space or a full-width space instead of ‘、’. Personally, for now, I prefer half-width spaces.
texts.もちろん文章の最後に打つ。『、』と違って、こちらに悩むことは少ないはず。ただ意識: Of course, you put it at the end of a sentence. Unlike ‘、’, this should be less confusing. However, you may not notice this unless you pay attention to it: in general novels, it has become common not to put ‘。’ at the end of dialogue enclosed in quotation marks. If you close dialogue with a quotation mark, it may be safest to follow this rule.
texts.明日も晴れるといいですね」: I hope it’s sunny tomorrow too.”
texts.三点リーダ『…』と棒ダッシュ『―』の使い方: How to Use the Ellipsis ‘…’ and Em Dash ‘―’
texts.一般的な小説のルールでは、『…』『―』共に偶数回連続で繋げて使用する。『……』『: According to the general rules for novels, both ‘…’ and ‘―’ are used consecutively an even number of times. For example: ‘……’, ‘…………’, ‘――’, and ‘――――’. In games and manga, however, you may also see ‘…’ used by itself.
texts.この２つの使い道に付いては、分かるようで分からない人も多いと思う。一部使い道が重: I think many people understand what these two are used for—or think they do—but are not completely sure. It is even more confusing because some of their uses overlap. So, I have compiled their uses below.
texts.語尾を濁す：「たぶん、そうだと思うけど……」: Trailing off: “I think that’s probably right, but……”
texts.『―』と比較すると、使い道が分かりやすいので、特に補足はいらないと思う。: Compared to “―,” its uses are easier to understand, so I don't think any particular explanation is necessary.
texts.割込：先生「え～と、何か連絡事項がある方は――」生徒「はい！」: Interruption: Teacher: “Um, if anyone has any announcements—” Student: “Yes!”
texts.引用：「この古文書によると――玉座の後ろを調べろ――とあるね」: Quotation: “According to this ancient document, it says—‘Search behind the throne’—you know.”
texts.補足：俺は村長の家――それは村中で最も立派な建物だった――に向かった。: Supplement: I headed for the village chief's house—it was the finest building in the village.
texts.『割込』は唯一『―』の安定した使いどころ。: “Interruption” is the only reliable use for “―.”
texts.『引用』は””や『』で囲ったほうが分かりやすいかも。: “Quotation” might be easier to understand if enclosed in quotation marks such as “ ” or ‘ ’.
texts.『補足』は文章の中に文章を挟む構造になる。（）と使い方が類似している。海外小説の: “Supplement” creates a structure in which one sentence is inserted into another. Its usage is similar to parentheses. You often see it in translations of foreign novels, but writing that uses it too much is difficult to read. Rather than use it excessively, it would probably be better to rethink the sentence structure. That said, it doesn't seem to have much to do with games.
texts.間を置く：「……それで、結局どうしますか？」: Pause: “……So, what are we going to do in the end?”
texts.文を繋ぐ：「神――いわゆるゴッドの思し召しなのです」: Connecting sentences: “God—it is the will of what is commonly called God.”
texts.『間を置く』の例のように文頭に間を作ることもできる。話題を転換したい場合などで有: As in the example under “Pause,” you can also create a pause at the beginning of a sentence. This is effective when, for example, you want to change the subject. Personally, I prefer expressing pauses with “…” or “―” because it gives the pacing a better flow than creating pauses with “Wait” processing for everything.
texts.『文を繋ぐ』は『、』に近い運用方法となる。溜めを作ることで、後の文章をより強調で: “Connecting sentences” is used in a way similar to a comma. Creating a buildup can also emphasize the sentence that follows.
texts.このパターンの場合、『…』『―』どちらでも良いのだけど、個人的な印象では『…』は: In this pattern, either “…” or “―” is fine, but personally, I feel that “…” seems weak, while “―” feels speedy. There is no clearly standardized distinction between the uses of “…” and “―”; it is fairly ambiguous. Their uses also vary from writer to writer. If you're interested, I recommend paying attention to this when reading professional writing.
texts.感嘆符『！』と疑問符『？』の使い方: How to use exclamation marks “!” and question marks “?”
texts.『…』『―』と比較して、こちらの使い道に悩む人は少ないと思うが、ついでに書いてみ: Compared to “…” and “―,” I don't think many people have trouble deciding how to use these, but I'll cover them while I'm at it.
texts.『！』は驚きや叫びを現す。「うわっ！」「お～い！！」など。２つ以上重ねて強調する: “!” expresses surprise or a shout, as in “Whoa!” or “Heeey!!” Two or more can also be repeated for emphasis. “?” expresses a question or confusion, as in “Who are you?” or “Huh?” Repeating it two or more times is less common.
texts.『！？』というように両方を合わせる方法も多用される。「おかしいだろ！？」「マジで: Combining both, as in “!?,” is also frequently used. In expressions such as “That's not right!?” and “Seriously!?,” it conveys confusion while shouting in surprise. “?!” is not used as often, but if you have a reason—such as wanting to emphasize confusion more than surprise or to show originality—then go ahead.
texts.「図書館では静かに……！」「へっ……？」「信じられない……！？」というように『…: They can also be combined with “…” as in “Quiet in the library……!”, “Huh……?”, or “Unbelievable……!?”. Some people may find it odd for “!” and “…”—which have nearly opposite meanings—to coexist, but I think the nuance is something like “not raising one's voice, but expressing strong emotion.” Probably……
texts.漢字で書くか、書かないか？: Should you write it in kanji or not?
texts.以下のような言葉は特に、人によって漢字で表記するか、ひらがなで表記するか意見が分: With words like the following in particular, opinions differ from person to person on whether to write them in kanji or hiragana. Try to keep your policy consistent as much as possible.
texts.筆者は『事』や『様』の使い方によく迷う。ひらがなが続く文章の場合は漢字で、漢字が: The writer often has trouble deciding how to use “thing” and “way.” When a sentence contains a long string of hiragana, I feel like typing them in kanji; when it contains a long string of kanji, I feel like typing them in hiragana. After writing all this, I have to admit that keeping things consistent is quite difficult. Perhaps it would be better to deliberately abandon consistency and go with the atmosphere or mood of the moment.
texts.例えば、『未曾有（みぞう）』『顰蹙（ひんしゅく）』『翻す（ひるがえす）』のような: For example, should you use difficult kanji for words such as “unprecedented (mizō),” “disapproval (hinshuku),” and “retract (hirugaesu)”? On a PC, it is easy to convert words into kanji, but converting everything automatically is worth reconsidering. Depending on the target age of your players, consider writing them in hiragana or katakana, such as “mizō” and “hinshuku.” However, be careful: wording such as “This is a mizō situation” looks unattractive.
texts.上記の様に、もう少し簡単な言葉に言い換える方法もある。フリガナを打てるならば、理: As shown above, you can also rephrase these with somewhat simpler words. Adding furigana would be ideal, but there are issues involving the limitations of the development tool and the extra effort required.
texts.読みやすい文章を書くためには、ルールの策定が不可欠。ウインドウの形状や文字色など: Establishing rules is essential for writing easy-to-read text. Using techniques unique to games, such as window shapes and text colors, is another option. In any case, establish your own rules. Be careful not to end up having to unify the formatting and writing style near the end of development.
